steps.description:
Write a python class named Racer with the following attributes:

Class Variable: track_length set it to 30. It represents the track length.

Object Variable: distance stores the distance travelled in a race

Functions: race() increase distance by 1 each time it is called. display() display position of racer on the screen with one space per unit travelled followed by R. reach() return True if distance equals to track_length else return False

Static Method: main() It will perform the following: 1. Create an object from the class. 2. Before the race starts: a. clear the screen b. call display() c. pause for 3 sec 3. Do the following repeatedly: a. clear the screen b. call race() c. call display() and pause for 0.5 sec d. call reach() and end program if it returns True

Run Racer.main().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint:

You may use the following command to clear the screen:

import os # For Windows os.system('cls') # For macOS and Linux os.system('clear')


Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

The race begins with R on the left R

the racer will race to the right R

and ends when it reaches track_length R

Certain cultures believe certain numbers are less lucky than others. The Chinese, for example, commonly consider 4 to be unlucky due to its Chinese pronunciation. You decided to investigate by creating a program to see if number 4 will always lose in a race.

Write a python class named Racer with the following attributes:

Class Variable: track_length set it to 30. It represents the track length.

Object Variables: racer_num stores the racer number distance stores the distance travelled in a race

Functions: race() add a random number (1 to 3) to distance each time it is called. if it exceeds track_length, set it to track_length. display() display position of racer on the screen with one space per unit travelled followed by racer_num and a " : " character at track_length spaces away if racer has not reached there.

Static Methods: winner(racer_list) takes in a list of Racer objects and determine the winners. A racer wins when its reaches the end point ":". If there are winners (can be more than 1), all winners will be displayed and True is returned. Otherwise it will return False. main() It will perform the following: 1. Create a list of 4 objects from the class with racer number 1 to 4. 2. Before the race starts: a. clear the screen b. call display() of each racer c. pause for 3 seconds. 3. Start the race by doing the following repeatedly: a. call race() of each racer. b. call display() of each racer and pause for 0.5 sec c. call winner(racer_list) to display winners if any d. end program when there is at least a winner

Run Racer.main().

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint:

You may use the following command to clear the screen:

import os # For Windows os.system('cls') # For macOS and Linux os.system('clear')

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Note that your results may differ as they are random.

The race begins like this 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 :

the racers will race towards the ":" 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 :

and ends when any racer reaches or surpass the end 1 : 2 3 : 4 Winner(s): Racer 2 Racer 4
